newsitem.title: UK: Two bombs rock English town after IRA warning-BBC.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs rock English town after IRA warning-BBC.

text.p: Two bombs exploded in the northwestern English town of Wilmslow early on Wednesday after a coded warning from the Irish Republican Army, BBC television reported.
It said there were no immediate reports of casualties after the devices exploded at the town's railway and police stations.

Local fire brigade spokesman Evan Morris told BBC radio that the first device had exploded at the railway station in Wilmslow, a town just to the south of Manchester airport, after a coded warning was given.

"We received reports there would be an explosion at Wilmslow station and shortly afterwards there was indeed an explosion. It would appear there was a secondary explosion shortly after 7 a.m.," he said.
Initial reports said the second blast had hit the town's police station.
Police rapidly sealed off the area around the railway station but there were no signs of immediate damage to the buildings.
The Irish Republican Army has set off several bombs on the English mainland since ending a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.
It was not clear whether the IRA might have timed a bombing campaign to coincide with Britain's forthcoming general election, which is due to be held for May 1.
One eyewitness reported two large explosions early in the morning.
"We were woken up by an enormous bang at 6.30 a.m," Bridget Hunt told the BBC.
"At 7 a.m. there was another even bigger explosion which rocked the ground...it was a terrific bang which shook the house," she said.
Last June the IRA detonated a huge device in the centre of Manchester which devastated a shopping precinct in the city, causing huge damage.

The devices exploded ahead of the Easter weekend, which is one of the most sacred dates for the IRA, since it marks the anniversary of a major republican uprising against British rule in Dublin in 1916.
